0.0.n: A conversational transition used to introduce what comes next.

0.2.n: Introduces the starting point of her recommendations.

0.3.n: Combined with の, it identifies the recommendation as the speaker’s.

0.4.n: Links 私 to おすすめ, marking whose recommendation it is.

0.5.n: This is part of とっても, a conversational intensifier; it is not a separate verb here.

0.6.n: Together with とって, this forms とっても; it does not mean also here.

0.7.n: おすすめの describes a place the speaker recommends.

0.8.n: Links おすすめ to 場所, letting the recommendation describe the place.

0.9.n: The following line identifies which location the speaker means.

1.0.n: 一つ counts one item; adding 目 makes it first in a sequence.

1.1.n: Marks 一つ目 as the topic: the item the speaker is about to identify.

1.3.n: A place name for a prefecture on Japan’s island of Shikoku.

1.5.n: The speaker repeats the same place name before finishing the sentence.

1.6.n: A polite sentence ending that identifies the first recommended place.

2.0.n: The past form of 聞く, used with こと to refer to a past experience.

2.1.n: Turns 聞いた into an experience that can be asked about with あります.

2.2.n: Marks the experience as the topic; が is also common in this pattern.

2.3.n: The polite form of ある; with a past verb plus こと, it expresses having had that experience.

2.4.n: Placed at the end to make this a polite question.

0.lit: So then, first, my very recommended place,
0.tip: とっても is one word meaning very, even though the subtitle splits it into two tappable pieces.

1.lit: As for the first one, Ehime Prefecture, it is Ehime Prefecture.
1.tip: Adding 目 to a counter turns a quantity into an order: 一つ目 means the first one.

2.lit: As for the experience of having heard, does it exist?
2.tip: A past-form verb plus ことがありますか asks whether someone has ever had that experience.
